setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (2 reviews): The reviewer's only clear memory is Help On The Way opening the second set; Remembers incredible guitar playing through the Help/Slipknot/Franklin's Tower sequence [18][20]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Feel Like A Stranger is singled out as a good version [24]
- **Friend of the Devil** (1 review): Friend of the Devil has a nice jam [22]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 other source): Brent scat sings at about 4:07 in Beat It On Down The Line [4]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Row Jimmy is also praised as a good version [24]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet has some nice solos and jams [24]

## The recordings

- **gd84-07-04.sbd.miller.27761.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 166 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1984-07-04.sbd.miller.bertha.27862.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Tape flutter and speed problems from machine trouble are audible throughout; noise reduction was applied to soften hiss [2]
- **gd1984-07-04.senn421.carpenter.andrewf.87341.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 164 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1984-07-04.150315.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 22 songs; 166 min [4]
- **gd84-07-04.senn421.braverman.14194.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 162 min; rated 4.53/5 by 17 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound quality is not great [22]

## Around the show

- Parked in a small lot directly across the street from the Five Seasons [18]
- Liked to roam the crowded arena during the first-set break to check out the venue [20]
- Saw Phil take a huge hit from a joint while standing near the stage during the break [21]
- Recalls Phil dedicating a song to Paul and the Rainbow Bus, rather than Bobby doing so [22]
- Believes Paul was killed in Indianapolis days earlier, hit by a car after stepping into the street [25]
- Doug spilled red wine in the car on the drive to Cedar Rapids, after the group had taken doses [25]
- Police were driving up and down the street busting people; the reviewer's friend was arrested for drinking beer outside [26]
- Claims Paul died en route to the show when a bus crashed outside St. Louis, gear landing on him [27]
- Judged a solid, slightly above-average mid-eighties show, neither among the best nor the worst [18]
- Calls it one of the most solid shows of the whole tour, with an outstanding first set [21]
- Ranked at the top of the tour, behind only the Friday the 13th full-moon Dark Star show [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd84-07-04.sbd.miller.27761.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Master Cassette> Cassette> Dat, plus patches from FOB Sennheiser 421> Cass [1]. Also: Transferred and patched by Charlie Miller via Sony R500 DAT; speed corrected by +2.37% to match the FOB patches [1]
- **gd1984-07-04.sbd.miller.bertha.27862.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: Bertha Remaster of the Master Cassette/Cassette source [2]. Also: Digitally remastered with a dual-DAW setup called Bertha, finished January 19, 2005 [2]
- **gd1984-07-04.senn421.carpenter.andrewf.87341.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F; source: Sennheiser MD-421's > patched thru one deck (D5?) > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XL-II's, with no Dolby. Mics on stand set up FOB [3]. Also: Patches from the ShnID-14194 Sennheiser 421 source cover all of Feel Like A Stranger, Don't Ease Me In, Good Lovin' and U.S. Blues; Levels, fades and patches done in Soundforge; TLH used for SBE-OK, FLAC compression and checksums [3]
- **gd1984-07-04.150315.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew - Tom Pinney, Sean Murtha; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: MAUD CA: Beyer M88's XY > Sony TCD5M|s1 Maxell UDXLIIS 90; s2 Maxell MX90 no NR, 2nd deck in line Location: 80 feet from stage DFC 7 feet up [4]. Also: Cuts occur where decks were flipped, including a quick mid-tape flip that may have missed about seven seconds [4]
- **gd84-07-04.senn421.braverman.14194.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD: MC (Sennheiser 421)> DAT> CD> SHN [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead July 4, 1984 - The Five Seasons Center](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/july-4-1984-five-seasons-center) [31]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1984-07-04 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-07-04-backstage-pass/) [32]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Five Seasons Center - July 4, 1984](https://www.dead.net/show/july-4-1984) [33]

Digitally remastered with a dual-DAW setup called Bertha, finished January 19, 2005
Tape flutter and speed problems from machine trouble are audible throughout; noise reduction was applied to soften hiss
Patches from the ShnID-14194 Sennheiser 421 source cover all of Feel Like A Stranger, Don't Ease Me In, Good Lovin' and U.S. Blues
Levels, fades and patches done in Soundforge; TLH used for SBE-OK, FLAC compression and checksums
